topic: Run your hand across your tire tread — feel that saw-tooth edge?
negativePromptStanding: faces, hands, human figures, on-screen text, logos, watermarks, subtitles

beats.narration: Run your hand across your tire tread — feel sharp on one side, smooth on the other?
beats.visualPrompt: Extreme macro shot of a tire tread block pattern under raking side light, texture strongly emphasized, static camera, no hand or tool in frame.

beats.narration: That saw-tooth feel is called feathering — it doesn't show up as a bulge or a crack, you have to feel for it.
beats.visualPrompt: Extreme macro of a single tread block edge in profile: one side crisp and sharp in shadow, the opposite side visibly rounded/worn smooth, hard side lighting, slow push-in.

beats.narration: One clue: it usually points to toe misalignment — the tires pointed slightly in or out instead of straight.
beats.visualPrompt: Undercarriage/wheel-well shot of a front tire and the visible steering knuckle/tie-rod area, static mounted camera, dim garage lighting.

beats.narration: But an alignment alone doesn't always fix it — a worn tie rod end or bushing can cause the same wear and needs replacing first.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up cutaway macro of a tie rod end and its rubber boot showing visible looseness/play, static mounted camera, dim garage light, no hands or tools in frame.

beats.narration: Don't guess which one it is. A quick check can point to the actual cause.
beats.visualPrompt: Close-up on an alignment-rack wheel clamp and sensor target mounted on a wheel in a shop bay, static camera, ambient shop lighting, no person in frame.

beats.narration: Worth checking before it eats through a new set of tires. Stop by and we'll take a look. Nick's Tire & Auto.
beats.visualPrompt: Branded end-card plate: Nick's Tire & Auto shop bay wide shot, warm daylight, static hold. Logo and CTA text composited in post, never AI-generated.

postingSpecs.feedCaption: Feel a saw-tooth edge across your tread? That's feathering — usually toe misalignment, but sometimes a worn tie rod that needs replacing before the alignment will hold. Stop by and we'll take a look.
